severity: REFRAMES THE STUDY -- per-condition outcomes are not reproducible
claim: For a fixed checkpoint, fixed frozen conditions and deterministic execution, the GRASP stage is perfectly reproducible across processes while the POST-GRASP outcome (lift/carry) is uncorrelated noise.

evidence.protocol: eval_checkpoint.py, deterministic, frozen 25-condition prefix, no frame capture in either run

refutes.previous_hypothesis: g1_piston_render_physics_divergence.json proposed that the renderer's mid-chunk camera reads perturbed contact physics.
refutes.why_refuted: A no-capture rerun in a fresh process reproduces 0 of 5 stored lifts, exactly like the capture-enabled render. Capture is not the cause -- neither run reproduces the other, with or without it.
refutes.status: the capture hypothesis is CLOSED as not-the-cause

implications: Per-condition claims about this task are not supportable. Only aggregate rates are, and only with an uncertainty band that reflects run-to-run variation, not just binomial sampling error.
The matched-condition comparison methodology is undermined: pairing SAC and RLPD on the same condition assumes the condition's outcome is a property of the policy, and post-grasp it is not.
The frozen 25/50-condition suite measures the policy far less precisely than the Wilson intervals suggest, because those intervals assume a fixed per-condition success probability.
Run-to-run variation is a THIRD variance source, alongside training-seed variance and evaluation-condition variance, and it was never budgeted for.
The carry differences that motivated the whole SAC-vs-RLPD comparison (0.36 vs 0.16 vs 0.12) are of the same magnitude as this single-checkpoint run-to-run swing (0.12 -> 0.20).
likely_mechanism: Contact-rich manipulation with a marginal grasp. GPU non-determinism in the VLM forward pass (bf16 autocast, non-deterministic kernels) perturbs the action chunk slightly; PhysX contact resolution amplifies a marginal grasp into a different macroscopic outcome. The chunk-boundary finger snap (see g1_piston_chunk_boundary_jitter.json, 13/22 boundaries above 0.5 rad) plausibly sits right at that margin.
required_next: Repeat-evaluation of a single checkpoint to measure the run-to-run distribution directly, so any reported rate carries an honest interval. Until then no SAC-vs-RLPD ordering, and no per-condition claim, is supportable.
